data.narrative:
Bright Machines, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Amar Hanspal and Lior Susan, has raised $300M+ to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparables: 1 public company and 8 private firms including same-stage peers Hadrian ($1.6B), Agile Robots ($1.0B), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B).

Two triangulation methods yield differentiated perspectives. The stage-progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $300M total raised proxy, implying a $510M valuation. The peer-median method benchmarks against the 3 same-sector, same-stage comparables, which show a median valuation of $1.0B with a range spanning $1.0B to $1.6B. The peer cohort explicitly establishes higher-end precedent within the robotics sector at this funding stage.

Synthesizing both approaches produces a triangulated range of $434M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $755M. The 166% spread reflects meaningful divergence between capital-efficiency benchmarking and peer-set positioning. Key uncertainties include Bright Machines' relative product maturity, customer traction metrics, and burn rate relative to peer cohort—factors that would determine positioning within or outside the peer median. The stage-progression method floor suggests downside protection, while the peer-median ceiling reflects competitive positioning in a capital-intensive sector.
